components.institution_label: Teaching Relief for Child Rearing for Ladder Faculty
components.description: A full-time ladder faculty member who bears or adopts a child (under six), or whose spouse does, and who is the primary caregiver, is relieved of teaching for one whole semester within the first year, without loss of salary.
components.faculty_group_note: A full-time member of the ladder faculty (ladder ranks: assistant professor, associate professor on term, associate professor with tenure, professor)
components.faculty_scope: all schools except the School of Medicine (Handbook XVII.D: 'The policies below apply in the rest of the University’s Schools'); includes the FAS (arts, sciences and the School of Engineering & Applied Science)
components.eligible_parent_wording: bears a child or adopts a child under the age of six or whose spouse bears a child or adopts a child under the age of six
components.caregiver_condition_wording: To qualify for this relief the faculty member must be a primary caregiver throughout the period of relief: personally caring for the child during normal working hours, while the other parent, if any, is employed at least half time.
components.entitlement_note: 'will be relieved of teaching duties': grant wording. Teaching relief is not a leave of absence, so the general leave condition XVII.A.1 ('Leave is a privilege, not a right') does not apply to it.
components.duration_note: 'for the whole of an academic semester'; the alternative of half relief over two semesters is c2.
components.pay_fraction: without loss of salary or benefits
components.time_window: within the first year after the birth or adoption; an adopted child must be under the age of six
components.dual_employee_rule: both parents full-time Yale ladder faculty may choose to divide the relief, each being granted one semester of relief from one half of the teaching responsibilities
components.relief_note: Teaching duties are relieved; 'Any other administrative and departmental responsibilities should be consistent with the purpose of the teaching relief'; XVII.D.6 asks for a schedule carrying out 'as many non-teaching responsibilities as are practicable'.

sequence.note: The texts do not order child-rearing teaching relief and the short-term-disability relief for the birth semester (XXI.E); XVII.D.3 cross-refers to XXI.E without stating that one replaces the other. Fully-paid teaching relief is 'available only once for each birth event'.

Not linked: the documents do not say whether the unpaid Child-Rearing Leave (c3) and the paid teaching relief (c1) may both be taken for one birth, or in what order; they are left unlinked (U3: leaves not added). III.F and XVII.A.8 list them as alternative triggers for the extension ('granted a Child-Rearing Leave or ... relief from teaching').

Statutes: Handbook XVII.A.1 'University leave policies incorporate the rights provided to employees under both federal and state Family Medical Leave Acts' → FMLA (c15) and CT FMLA (c16), both verified against the statute texts (2026_00/2026_01; 2018_30 2017 revision). CT FMLA applies to employers of 75 or more employees; that Yale meets this is assumed (not stated in the documents).

Calendar: the Handbook uses semesters ('In the case of a semester’s leave, the period of leave is one-half of the academic year') without stating a length: calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.

No leave_limits entry: XVII.A.5 'The maximum period of a leave is one academic year' and XVII.A.7 (no more than four semesters of leave in seven years, exceptions considered for child rearing) are per-leave or multi-year limits not binding on a single birth's leaves; the Caregivers Leave reduction by Child-Rearing Leave time goes in c4's duration_note (schema §1, Yale example).
